{{Short description|American statistician}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=April 2021}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=April 2021}}
'''Miriam''' ('''Miki''') '''Gasko Donoho''' (also published as '''Miriam Gasko-Green''') is an American statistician whose research topics have included [[data visualization]],{{ran|A}}{{r|dynamic}} equivalences between [[binary regression]] and [[survival analysis]],{{ran|B}}{{r|jewell}} and [[robust regression]].{{ran|C}}{{r|mosler}}

==Education and career==
Gasko completed her Ph.D. in statistics at [[Harvard University]] in 1981.{{r|harv}} Her dissertation was ''Testing Sequentially Selected Outliers from Linear Models''.{{r|diss}} She became a professor of marketing and quantitative studies in the College of Business at [[San Jose State University]],{{r|treasurer}} director of the Silicon Valley Consumer Confidence Survey,{{r|confidence}} and treasurer of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].{{r|treasurer}}

==Recognition==
She is a Fellow of the Institute of Mathematical Statistics.{{r|fims}}
MacSpin, a program for three-dimensional data visualization that she developed with her husband [[David Donoho]] and brother-in-law Andrew Donoho, was named as the best scientific/engineering software of 1987 by ''[[MacUser]]'' magazine.{{r|macspin}}
